tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

schema.name: ScheduleWakeup
schema.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Write
tools.description:
Writes a file to the local filesystem.

Usage:
- This tool will overwrite the existing file if there is one at the provided path.
- If this is an existing file, you MUST use the Read tool first to read the file's contents. This tool will fail if you did not read the file first.
- Prefer the Edit tool for modifying existing files — it only sends the diff. Only use this tool to create new files or for complete rewrites.
- NEVER create documentation files (*.md) or README files unless explicitly requested by the User.
- Only use emojis if the user explicitly requests it. Avoid writing emojis to files unless asked.

1	# Cerne — Requirements and Screen Flow
2	
3	Cerne is a reflective-journaling mobile app with an AI assistant. The user records their day by text, audio or photo; a conversational agent consults those records (semantic search) to answer with context and to offer insights.
4	
5	This document is the product specification. The visual reference is the prototype in `docs/input/prototype/`; the backend API is documented in `docs/input/backend/`.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## 1. Functional requirements
10	
11	### RF01 — Multimodal capture (text / audio / photo)
12	Data entry by text, real-time audio recording and photo upload — always through Screen 2 (Insertion Modal), which has a raw text field in addition to the microphone and the gallery. Every capture becomes a persisted record (`POST /entries`), **distinct from a chat message** (see the separation note in RF04).
13	
14	**Acceptance criteria:**
15	- The three modalities (text, audio, photo) result in the same persisted-entry format — none is treated structurally differently from the others after capture.
16	- Cancelling a capture midway (e.g., interrupting a recording) does not create a partial or empty entry.
17	
18	### RF02 — Speech-to-text / OCR processing
19	Transcription of audio (speech-to-text) and recognition of text in images (OCR) over the content captured in RF01.
20	
21	**Acceptance criteria:** four visible states — recording, processing, transcribed, transcription error.
22	
23	### RF03 — Biometric authentication vault
24	Access barrier via Face ID / Touch ID / PIN before exposing the user's data.
25	
26	**Acceptance criteria:**
27	- A biometric failure (e.g., fingerprint not recognized) offers PIN as an alternative, without locking the user out of the app.
28	- The app, sent to the background and resumed after 5 minutes, requires authentication again — it does not stay unlocked indefinitely (fixed value, not configurable by the user).
29	
30	### RF04 — Interactive chat with memory (RAG)
31	Continuous conversation with the AI agent, with semantic search over previous entries. **Chat messages are conversational and do not create journal entries automatically** — the only exception is the explicit save action described in RF10. Otherwise, the chat queries existing entries via RAG but does not write to them.
32	
33	**Acceptance criteria:**
34	- Three mandatory UI states: processing/streaming, error, complete response.
35	- If the response stream drops midway, the partial message stays visible with a failure indication (it does not disappear).
36	
37	### RF05 — Personal summary export
38	Generation of a narrative summary by AI (Claude Haiku 4.5) from the user's entries, exportable as PDF, with an additional option to download the raw data without the narrative. No clinical or diagnostic connotation. **Scope: job generation, file download and failure handling — never the quality of the generated narrative text.**
39	
40	**Acceptance criteria:**
41	- An export job with zero entries in the period returns a handled error state (not an empty PDF, not a crash).
42	- A failure generating the narrative text (model timeout) still allows downloading the raw data without the narrative — the export is not blocked by an AI failure.
43	
44	### RF06 — Semantic search / filter over journal entries
45	Semantic similarity search (via Voyage AI embeddings, reusing the ones already generated in RF01) combined with metadata filters (date, entry type). There is no filter by tag or category: the backend does not implement it in any endpoint — `GET /entries` and `GET /entries/search` accept only `source` and `dateFrom`/`dateTo`. Tags appear only embedded, read-only, in the `Entry` object (see section 2).
46	
47	**Acceptance criteria:**
48	- Searching for a term finds semantically related entries even without the exact word (e.g., searching "ansiedade" returns an entry that only mentions "nervosismo", without the literal term).
49	- 300 ms search debounce: fast typing triggers a single query, not one per keystroke.
50	- Results from the local read cache stay consistent with the server after reconnection, without duplicating displayed items *(the architecture is cloud-only; offline allows only viewing already-cached data, not writing)*.
51	- Two or more filters applied at the same time (`source` + `dateFrom`/`dateTo`) narrow results with AND logic (not OR).
52	- Clearing the filters returns to the full list without restarting the screen.
53	
54	### RF07 — Multi-source history (timeline)
55	A screen whose state depends simultaneously on authentication, synchronization status and entry data.
56	
57	**Acceptance criteria:**
58	- Session expiration while viewing triggers a new-login prompt without a crash and without losing the scroll position.
59	- The per-entry synchronization status badge updates independently of the authentication stream.
60	- No BLoC imports another BLoC directly.
61	
62	### RF08 — Proactive insights (mechanism)
63	A suggestion inserted into the chat without the user asking for it. **Scope: only the trigger mechanism, never the quality of the generated text.**
64	
65	**Acceptance criteria:**
66	- Trigger after N = 5 user messages OR T = 2 min of inactivity — fires exactly once per satisfied condition.
67	- If insight generation fails (timeout / network error), the main chat keeps working normally.
68	- Dismissing the insight does not change the scroll position or the state of the main conversation.
69	
70	### RF09 — Temporal summaries / dashboard
71	An evolution chart with a textual summary, computed on demand when the Settings tab is opened. **Scope: aggregation and rendering, never the quality of the narrative text.**
72	
73	**Acceptance criteria:**
74	- Renders correctly in three scenarios: zero entries, one entry, more than 30 entries.
75	- The aggregation recalculates correctly after an entry is created (cache-invalidation test). Entries are immutable: there is no `PATCH /entries/:id` or `DELETE /entries/:id` in the backend, and no screen describes an edit or delete action on an entry.
76	- The AI narrative text is checked only for not breaking the UI in extreme cases — never for its content.
77	
78	### RF10 — Save a chat message as an entry
79	A button on each user message in the chat that converts it into a persisted entry — for moments when the user states relevant information during the conversation, not only through dedicated capture (RF01). It reuses the same `POST /entries` pipeline (PII check + embedding), with the origin marked as `chat`.
80	
81	**Acceptance criteria:**
82	- The chat feature triggers the creation of the entry through a shared interface / use case, never by directly importing a repository or data source of the entries feature — a violation here also breaks RNF06.
83	- Saving the same message twice does not create duplicate entries (idempotency).
84	- A failure to save (network unavailable) keeps the conversation working normally, and the button returns to a state that allows trying again — the same failure-isolation pattern as RF08.
85	- Only user messages have the button — AI responses cannot become entries.
86	
87	---
88	
89	## 2. Extension features — not implemented
90	
91	They keep the "essence" of the original product flow and exist in the prototype, but **receive no functional implementation**. A menu entry may exist as a placeholder.
92	
93	| Original feature | Treatment in the current version |
94	|---|---|
95	| Dynamic categorization (AI) | Simplified to manual tags created by the user (My Records screen) |
96	| Autonomous goal extraction | Action Plans screen — static, no logic |
97	| Dynamic persona adjustment | Simple cosmetic toggle (Settings), low cost to maintain |
98	
99	---
100	
101	## 3. Quality requirements
102	
103	| ID | Requirement | Target |
104	|---|---|---|
105	| RNF06 | Zero layer violations — the domain layer does not import `package:flutter` nor classes from `data/` | 0 violations |
106	| RNF07 | Minimum test coverage of the domain layer (`lib/**/domain/**`) | ≥ 80% |
107	| RNF08 | Visual fidelity to the prototype — the primary color matches the prototype's hex value, typography matches family and size, spacing matches the prototype; no visual value hardcoded outside the central file `design_tokens.dart` | Every screen faithful in color, typography and spacing; 0 hardcoded values |
108	| RNF09 | Consistent network-error handling — `Either<Failure, T>` pattern via `fpdart` in every repository; every write endpoint (5 endpoints) handles three failure types — timeout, malformed response, no connection — covered by tests with `mocktail` | 0 repository signatures outside the pattern; 15 of 15 scenarios handled |
109	
110	## 4. Other non-functional requirements
111	
112	RNF01 — Interaction latency (a local action is reflected in the UI in < 100 ms; any network call above 300 ms shows a loading indicator) · RNF02 — PII stripping (via Claude Haiku 4.5 with a structured prompt / tool use, not a dedicated NER model) · RNF03 — Zero data retention · RNF04 — RLS (Row Level Security) · RNF05 — Hard delete of account and data (LGPD).
113	
114	**Known limitation:** the system has no protocol for detecting or responding to risk signals (suicidal ideation, self-harm) in entries or chat messages. Since the product is not framed as a mental-health app, this absence is an explicit scope decision.
115	
116	---
117	
118	## 5. Interface architecture and screen flow
119	
120	### 5.1 Visual foundation (design system)
121	Minimalist identity, a warm and neutral palette, readable sans-serif typography, standardized components (buttons, chat bubbles, cards). This foundation is the direct object of RNF08. Tokens: `docs/input/prototype/prototype-extract.md`.
122	
123	### 5.2 Screens
124	
125	**Screen 0 — Splash:** initial loading; checks the connection and syncs the cache in the background. *Connects to: RF06, RNF01.*
126	
127	**Screen 0.1 — Authentication vault:** biometric/PIN barrier before access. *Connects to: RF03.*
128	
129	**Screen 1 — Home (chat):** main screen, continuous conversation, "+" button for multimodal input, AI status indicator, "save to journal" button on each user message. *Connects to: RF04, RF08, RF10, RNF01, RNF09.*
130	
131	**Screen 2 — Insertion Modal:** overlay with three ways to capture — raw text field, microphone (audio) and gallery/camera (photo) — with a transcription indicator. Every capture here creates a persisted entry, never a chat message. *Connects to: RF01, RF02.*
132	
133	**Screen 3 — Side menu (sidebar):** navigation hub, session history, access to My Records / Action Plans / Settings, and a "Novo Chat" button that opens Screen 1 in its empty state. *Connects to: RF04 (via the "Novo Chat" button); the other items are pure navigation.*
134	
135	**Screen 4 — My Records:** consolidated timeline, filters, manual tags (extension, section 2), export. *Connects to: RF07, RF06, RF05.*
136	
137	**Screen 5 — Action Plans:** simple Kanban board (columns "A Fazer" / "Em Andamento" / "Concluído") with static example cards. *(Extension — section 2.)*
138	
139	**Screen 6 — Settings and profile:** evolution dashboard, persona selector — "Analítico" / "Empático" / "Socrático" (extension, section 2; it would only change the system-prompt string of RF04), delete account. *Connects to: RF09, RNF05.*
140	
141	---
142	
143	## 6. Backend endpoint inventory
144	
145	The backend is already built and frozen. The API contract, `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`, is the source of truth; this section is a reading of it oriented by screen and requirement. How to build the real URL of each operation: `docs/input/backend/README.md`.
146	
147	Every endpoint returns errors in the standard contract of RNF09 — `{ code, message, retryable }` — and is protected by RLS in Supabase. AI providers: Claude (chat, vision/OCR, summary, insights, dashboard, PII detection) and Voyage AI (embeddings) — the backend's only two external AI dependencies. Audio transcription (speech-to-text) runs on-device (Whisper) and never reaches the backend as an audio file.
148	
149	### 6.1 Authentication and session
150	| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
151	|---|---|---|

# Cerne — Requirements and Screen Flow

Cerne is a reflective-journaling mobile app with an AI assistant. The user records their day by text, audio or photo; a conversational agent consults those records (semantic search) to answer with context and to offer insights.

This document is the product specification. The visual reference is the prototype in `docs/input/prototype/`; the backend API is documented in `docs/input/backend/`.

---

## 1. Functional requirements

### RF01 — Multimodal capture (text / audio / photo)
Data entry by text, real-time audio recording and photo upload — always through Screen 2 (Insertion Modal), which has a raw text field in addition to the microphone and the gallery. Every capture becomes a persisted record (`POST /entries`), **distinct from a chat message** (see the separation note in RF04).

**Acceptance criteria:**
- The three modalities (text, audio, photo) result in the same persisted-entry format — none is treated structurally differently from the others after capture.
- Cancelling a capture midway (e.g., interrupting a recording) does not create a partial or empty entry.

### RF02 — Speech-to-text / OCR processing
Transcription of audio (speech-to-text) and recognition of text in images (OCR) over the content captured in RF01.

**Acceptance criteria:** four visible states — recording, processing, transcribed, transcription error.

### RF03 — Biometric authentication vault
Access barrier via Face ID / Touch ID / PIN before exposing the user's data.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- A biometric failure (e.g., fingerprint not recognized) offers PIN as an alternative, without locking the user out of the app.
- The app, sent to the background and resumed after 5 minutes, requires authentication again — it does not stay unlocked indefinitely (fixed value, not configurable by the user).

### RF04 — Interactive chat with memory (RAG)
Continuous conversation with the AI agent, with semantic search over previous entries. **Chat messages are conversational and do not create journal entries automatically** — the only exception is the explicit save action described in RF10. Otherwise, the chat queries existing entries via RAG but does not write to them.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Three mandatory UI states: processing/streaming, error, complete response.
- If the response stream drops midway, the partial message stays visible with a failure indication (it does not disappear).

### RF05 — Personal summary export
Generation of a narrative summary by AI (Claude Haiku 4.5) from the user's entries, exportable as PDF, with an additional option to download the raw data without the narrative. No clinical or diagnostic connotation. **Scope: job generation, file download and failure handling — never the quality of the generated narrative text.**

**Acceptance criteria:**
- An export job with zero entries in the period returns a handled error state (not an empty PDF, not a crash).
- A failure generating the narrative text (model timeout) still allows downloading the raw data without the narrative — the export is not blocked by an AI failure.

### RF06 — Semantic search / filter over journal entries
Semantic similarity search (via Voyage AI embeddings, reusing the ones already generated in RF01) combined with metadata filters (date, entry type). There is no filter by tag or category: the backend does not implement it in any endpoint — `GET /entries` and `GET /entries/search` accept only `source` and `dateFrom`/`dateTo`. Tags appear only embedded, read-only, in the `Entry` object (see section 2).

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Searching for a term finds semantically related entries even without the exact word (e.g., searching "ansiedade" returns an entry that only mentions "nervosismo", without the literal term).
- 300 ms search debounce: fast typing triggers a single query, not one per keystroke.
- Results from the local read cache stay consistent with the server after reconnection, without duplicating displayed items *(the architecture is cloud-only; offline allows only viewing already-cached data, not writing)*.
- Two or more filters applied at the same time (`source` + `dateFrom`/`dateTo`) narrow results with AND logic (not OR).
- Clearing the filters returns to the full list without restarting the screen.

### RF07 — Multi-source history (timeline)
A screen whose state depends simultaneously on authentication, synchronization status and entry data.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Session expiration while viewing triggers a new-login prompt without a crash and without losing the scroll position.
- The per-entry synchronization status badge updates independently of the authentication stream.
- No BLoC imports another BLoC directly.

### RF08 — Proactive insights (mechanism)
A suggestion inserted into the chat without the user asking for it. **Scope: only the trigger mechanism, never the quality of the generated text.**

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Trigger after N = 5 user messages OR T = 2 min of inactivity — fires exactly once per satisfied condition.
- If insight generation fails (timeout / network error), the main chat keeps working normally.
- Dismissing the insight does not change the scroll position or the state of the main conversation.

### RF09 — Temporal summaries / dashboard
An evolution chart with a textual summary, computed on demand when the Settings tab is opened. **Scope: aggregation and rendering, never the quality of the narrative text.**

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Renders correctly in three scenarios: zero entries, one entry, more than 30 entries.
- The aggregation recalculates correctly after an entry is created (cache-invalidation test). Entries are immutable: there is no `PATCH /entries/:id` or `DELETE /entries/:id` in the backend, and no screen describes an edit or delete action on an entry.
- The AI narrative text is checked only for not breaking the UI in extreme cases — never for its content.

### RF10 — Save a chat message as an entry
A button on each user message in the chat that converts it into a persisted entry — for moments when the user states relevant information during the conversation, not only through dedicated capture (RF01). It reuses the same `POST /entries` pipeline (PII check + embedding), with the origin marked as `chat`.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- The chat feature triggers the creation of the entry through a shared interface / use case, never by directly importing a repository or data source of the entries feature — a violation here also breaks RNF06.
- Saving the same message twice does not create duplicate entries (idempotency).
- A failure to save (network unavailable) keeps the conversation working normally, and the button returns to a state that allows trying again — the same failure-isolation pattern as RF08.
- Only user messages have the button — AI responses cannot become entries.

---

## 2. Extension features — not implemented

They keep the "essence" of the original product flow and exist in the prototype, but **receive no functional implementation**. A menu entry may exist as a placeholder.

| Original feature | Treatment in the current version |
|---|---|
| Dynamic categorization (AI) | Simplified to manual tags created by the user (My Records screen) |
| Autonomous goal extraction | Action Plans screen — static, no logic |
| Dynamic persona adjustment | Simple cosmetic toggle (Settings), low cost to maintain |

---

## 3. Quality requirements

| ID | Requirement | Target |
|---|---|---|
| RNF06 | Zero layer violations — the domain layer does not import `package:flutter` nor classes from `data/` | 0 violations |
| RNF07 | Minimum test coverage of the domain layer (`lib/**/domain/**`) | ≥ 80% |
| RNF08 | Visual fidelity to the prototype — the primary color matches the prototype's hex value, typography matches family and size, spacing matches the prototype; no visual value hardcoded outside the central file `design_tokens.dart` | Every screen faithful in color, typography and spacing; 0 hardcoded values |
| RNF09 | Consistent network-error handling — `Either<Failure, T>` pattern via `fpdart` in every repository; every write endpoint (5 endpoints) handles three failure types — timeout, malformed response, no connection — covered by tests with `mocktail` | 0 repository signatures outside the pattern; 15 of 15 scenarios handled |

## 4. Other non-functional requirements

RNF01 — Interaction latency (a local action is reflected in the UI in < 100 ms; any network call above 300 ms shows a loading indicator) · RNF02 — PII stripping (via Claude Haiku 4.5 with a structured prompt / tool use, not a dedicated NER model) · RNF03 — Zero data retention · RNF04 — RLS (Row Level Security) · RNF05 — Hard delete of account and data (LGPD).

**Known limitation:** the system has no protocol for detecting or responding to risk signals (suicidal ideation, self-harm) in entries or chat messages. Since the product is not framed as a mental-health app, this absence is an explicit scope decision.

---

## 5. Interface architecture and screen flow

### 5.1 Visual foundation (design system)
Minimalist identity, a warm and neutral palette, readable sans-serif typography, standardized components (buttons, chat bubbles, cards). This foundation is the direct object of RNF08. Tokens: `docs/input/prototype/prototype-extract.md`.

### 5.2 Screens

**Screen 0 — Splash:** initial loading; checks the connection and syncs the cache in the background. *Connects to: RF06, RNF01.*

**Screen 0.1 — Authentication vault:** biometric/PIN barrier before access. *Connects to: RF03.*

**Screen 1 — Home (chat):** main screen, continuous conversation, "+" button for multimodal input, AI status indicator, "save to journal" button on each user message. *Connects to: RF04, RF08, RF10, RNF01, RNF09.*

**Screen 2 — Insertion Modal:** overlay with three ways to capture — raw text field, microphone (audio) and gallery/camera (photo) — with a transcription indicator. Every capture here creates a persisted entry, never a chat message. *Connects to: RF01, RF02.*

**Screen 3 — Side menu (sidebar):** navigation hub, session history, access to My Records / Action Plans / Settings, and a "Novo Chat" button that opens Screen 1 in its empty state. *Connects to: RF04 (via the "Novo Chat" button); the other items are pure navigation.*

**Screen 4 — My Records:** consolidated timeline, filters, manual tags (extension, section 2), export. *Connects to: RF07, RF06, RF05.*

**Screen 5 — Action Plans:** simple Kanban board (columns "A Fazer" / "Em Andamento" / "Concluído") with static example cards. *(Extension — section 2.)*

**Screen 6 — Settings and profile:** evolution dashboard, persona selector — "Analítico" / "Empático" / "Socrático" (extension, section 2; it would only change the system-prompt string of RF04), delete account. *Connects to: RF09, RNF05.*

---

The backend is already built and frozen. The API contract, `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`, is the source of truth; this section is a reading of it oriented by screen and requirement. How to build the real URL of each operation: `docs/input/backend/README.md`.

---

## 8. Data model (reference)

Main entities of the backend (Supabase / Postgres). Field names are reference suggestions, not mandatory character by character. **Where this table differs from the API contract (`docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`), the contract prevails** (see section 6).

| Table | Main fields | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `users` | id, email, biometric_enabled, persona, created_at | RLS: a user accesses only their own row |
| `entries` | id, user_id, content, source (`manual`/`audio`/`photo`/`chat`), chat_message_id (nullable), embedding (vector, see 9), sync_status, created_at, updated_at | `embedding` generated in `POST /entries` via Voyage AI |
| `tags` | id, user_id, name | Extension — created manually by the user |
| `entry_tags` | entry_id, tag_id | N:N join table |
| `chat_sessions` | id, user_id, title, created_at | — |
| `chat_messages` | id, session_id, role (`user`/`assistant`), content, created_at | User messages show the RF10 button |
| `export_jobs` | id, user_id, status (`pending`/`processing`/`done`/`error`), period_start, period_end, file_url, created_at | Asynchronous — see 6.5 |

**RLS pattern (every table with `user_id`):** policy `auth.uid() = user_id`, no exceptions.

---

## 9. Technology stack

| Layer | Choice |
|---|---|
| Mobile app | Flutter, BLoC, Clean Architecture |
| Backend | Already built and frozen; consumed through its API |
| Infrastructure | Supabase (Postgres + pgvector + Storage + Auth + RLS) |
| Chat / vision / OCR / summary / insights / dashboard / PII | Claude Sonnet 5 (chat) + Claude Haiku 4.5 (the rest) — in the backend |
| Embeddings (RAG) | Voyage AI `voyage-4` — in the backend |
| Speech-to-text (audio transcription) | Whisper on-device (`whisper_ggml`); audio never reaches the backend |
| Error handling | `fpdart` (`Either<Failure, T>`) |
| Layer rule | RNF06 |
| Test coverage | RNF07 |

---

## 10. Configuration parameters

Fixed values — not to be reinterpreted.

| Parameter | Value | Requirement |
|---|---|---|
| Background session timeout | 5 min | RF03 |
| Search debounce | 300 ms | RF06 |
| Proactive insight trigger | 5 messages OR 2 min of inactivity | RF08 |
| Dashboard rendering scenarios | 0 / 1 / > 30 entries | RF09 |
| Minimum test coverage (domain) | ≥ 80% | RNF07 |
| Local UI latency | < 100 ms | RNF01 |
| Loading-indicator threshold | > 300 ms | RNF01 |
| Network-error scenarios tested | 5 endpoints × 3 failures = 15 | RNF09 |

---

## 11. Error codes (RNF09)

Every endpoint returns `{ code, message, retryable }`. Minimum codes the app handles:

| Code | Situation | `retryable` |
|---|---|---|
| `AUTH_EXPIRED` | Session expired, re-authentication needed | no |
| `AUTH_INVALID` | Invalid credentials / biometrics | no |
| `NETWORK_TIMEOUT` | Request exceeded the time limit | yes |
| `NETWORK_OFFLINE` | No connection — action blocked (see RF04/RF06) | yes |
| `VALIDATION_ERROR` | Malformed request body | no |
| `PII_CHECK_FAILED` | PII check failed before persisting | yes |
| `EMBEDDING_FAILED` | Voyage AI unavailable / error | yes |
| `AI_GENERATION_TIMEOUT` | Claude did not respond in time (chat/insight/summary/dashboard) | yes |
| `NOT_FOUND` | Resource does not exist or does not belong to the user | no |
| `RATE_LIMITED` | Request limit exceeded | yes |

The complete, closed list of the backend's 13 codes, with HTTP statuses, is in `docs/input/backend/error-taxonomy.md`.

---

## 12. Delivery order

Work is delivered in units, one per functional requirement, preceded by a foundation unit, in this order:

**F000 → RF03 → RF01 → RF02 → RF07 → RF06 → RF04 → RF10 → RF08 → RF05 → RF09**

- **F000 (foundation)** covers what no single requirement owns but all of them use: project scaffold, `design_tokens.dart`, HTTP client returning `Either`, login and sign-up (Screen 0.1a in the prototype), base navigation and expired-session handling.
- RF10 comes after RF01 and RF04; RF08 comes after RF04.

---

## 13. Technical constraints

**Fixed:**
- Flutter and Dart at the version pinned for the repository (fvm).
- State management: `flutter_bloc`.
- Clean Architecture, three layers per feature.
- Error handling: `fpdart`; repositories return `Either<Failure, T>`.
- Test doubles: `mocktail`.
- On-device speech-to-text: `whisper_ggml`.
- Visual tokens: `lib/core/design_tokens.dart` is the single source of colors, typography, spacing and radii.
- Platform: iOS, portrait only.
- Folder convention:

```
lib/
  core/
  features/
    <feature>/
      data/
      domain/
      presentation/
```

**Free (choose what fits):** routing, HTTP client, local cache, dependency injection, secure storage, biometrics package, chart package.

4

6	|---|---|---|

9

11	1. **Synchronizing** — the app has a local write not yet confirmed by the server (it has not yet received the response with the new `updatedAt`/`serverRevision`).
12	2. **Synchronization error** — the write was attempted and failed (network, or one of the 13 codes of the error taxonomy) and the app has not yet been able to reconcile.
13	3. **Synchronized** — the last confirmed write matched; nothing is pending on the client side for that entry.
14	
15	When to show each state is not decided by the server: the reconciliation logic lives in the client, using exactly these two fields.

# Synchronization badge semantics

There is no `sync_status` column in the database: the architecture is cloud-only, so "it is on the server" already means "synchronized", by definition. The server neither stores nor computes a synchronization state; it only exposes two fields, and the **badge is derived entirely in the app** from them:

| Field | Where it appears in the contract | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `updatedAt` | `Entry.updatedAt` | Timestamp of the last server write for that entry. |
| `serverRevision` | `Entry.serverRevision`, and also in the profile | Counter that increases with every write to the user's entries — never resets, never decreases. |

**The badge's 3 states, all inferred on the client — none comes ready from the server:**
1. **Synchronizing** — the app has a local write not yet confirmed by the server (it has not yet received the response with the new `updatedAt`/`serverRevision`).
2. **Synchronization error** — the write was attempted and failed (network, or one of the 13 codes of the error taxonomy) and the app has not yet been able to reconcile.
3. **Synchronized** — the last confirmed write matched; nothing is pending on the client side for that entry.

When to show each state is not decided by the server: the reconciliation logic lives in the client, using exactly these two fields.

content.content:
12:This PRD defines the product the Cerne Flutter app must become, built on `docs/input/requirements.md` (the frozen product specification), `docs/input/prototype/` (the frozen visual/screen reference), and `docs/input/backend/` (the frozen, already-built API contract). It also builds on three prior planning artifacts for this project — a product brief, a Working-Backwards PRFAQ, and an F000 technical-decisions forge session — without duplicating them; where those documents already settled something, this PRD states the conclusion and points back rather than re-deriving it. Implementation-level rationale (package choices, rejected alternatives, market-sizing detail, regulatory citations) lives in `addendum.md`, not here.
14:The document is structured so downstream work — UX specification, architecture, and epic/story breakdown — can reference it by stable ID: Functional Requirements are numbered globally (FR-1 through FR-43) regardless of which feature section they sit in, User Journeys are numbered UJ-1 through UJ-6, and Success Metrics SM-1 onward. Terms introduced in §3 Glossary are used verbatim everywhere else in this document.
16:Audience: the solo author, acting across PM/UX/architecture/dev roles for this capstone (TCC) project, and the academic reviewers who evaluate it. `[ASSUMPTION: ...]` tags mark places this PRD inferred something the source documents left unstated; see §9 for the full index.
26:Within this project's boundary, "done" means a working, fully tested iOS app that proves the RAG-memory differentiator end-to-end against the real (frozen) backend — covering capture, processing, chat, search, export, and account management — while leaving three named extension features (§5) as inert placeholders rather than attempting partial, half-working versions of them.
82:  - **Path:** selects a period → export sheet shows "Pendente" → "Processando" → either "Concluído" (both PDF narrative and raw data downloadable) or, if only the AI narrative step failed, raw data remains downloadable while the narrative is marked unavailable — the job is never blocked end-to-end by a narrative failure.
108:## Information Architecture
117:*Where an FR's testable condition is a single, self-evident clause, it is folded into the FR's statement itself rather than broken out into a separate Consequences block; the separate block is used once an FR needs more than one distinct, checkable condition.*
258:- The badge's update stream runs independently of the auth/session stream — a pending sync-badge transition is never blocked, delayed, or cleared by session-expiry handling (FR-17).
277:**Feature-specific NFRs:** No BLoC in this feature imports another BLoC directly — the three streams this screen composes (auth status, Sync Badge state, and Entry data) combine only through the domain layer, never via a direct BLoC-to-BLoC reference.
330:- `POST /chat/sessions` is blocked offline — starting a new Chat Session requires connectivity, consistent with the offline composer lock on existing conversations (FR-27).
396:Raw data is downloadable via `GET /export/:jobId/download` as soon as it's ready, even if the AI narrative step is still processing, has failed, or was skipped — the narrative never blocks the data download.
414:A separate narrative text is fetched via `GET /dashboard/narrative`; its failure is a distinct, chart-still-renders state, never blocking the chart (two independent endpoints by design).
464:- **SM-1**: Every acceptance criterion stated per-RF in requirements.md §1 passes. Validates FR-1 through FR-43, the feature-specific NFRs called out in §4 (e.g. the BLoC-composition rule under §4.5 FR-18), and RNF01's performance thresholds (manual timing spot-check per module, not automated).
465:- **SM-2**: Zero Clean Architecture layer violations (RNF06) and ≥80% domain-layer test coverage (RNF07), verified across all 11 feature modules.
478:1. **No project timeline, deadline, or defense date is stated anywhere in the source documents.** This blocks any confident sequencing/pacing judgment for downstream epics work. *(Flagged by the PRFAQ distillate as the single biggest open input.)*
479:2. **Signup field set is underspecified.** The prototype shows one screen toggled between Entrar/Criar conta with only email+password fields visible — no password confirmation, no display-name capture at signup. Confirm this is intentional before building FR-1. *(blocks F000 — build unit 1 of 11)*
480:3. **Tab-switching mid-capture in the Insertion Modal is undefined** (e.g., switching from Áudio to Foto while a recording is in progress) — decide: discard, warn, or persist the in-progress capture (affects FR-11). *(blocks RF01 — build unit 3 of 11)*
481:4. **No "account deleted" or "signed out" confirmation screen exists** — both flows dead-end at the Biometric Vault screen. Decide whether this is acceptable for v1 or needs even a lightweight confirmation (affects FR-42/FR-43). *(blocks RF09 — build unit 11 of 11; lowest urgency of the sequenced OQs)*
483:6. **The Sync Badge error state has no visible retry affordance in the current prototype** — decide whether the badge needs one, or whether reconciliation on the next successful write is sufficient (affects FR-15). *(blocks RF07 — build unit 5 of 11)*
484:7. **Combined search + filter behavior is unspecified** — when both a search term and active filters are set, decide the intended interaction (AND-combine vs. one overriding the other) (affects FR-19/FR-20). *(blocks RF06 — build unit 6 of 11)*
487:10. **Whether RF04's chat-response quality, and separately RF06's search-result quality, should carry the same "mechanism only, never graded" boundary that requirements.md states explicitly for RF05/RF08/RF09 is unstated for both.** Treated here as a genuine gap for each, not silently extended or silently dropped (§5, §Constraints and Guardrails). *(blocks grading boundary for RF04 — build unit 7 of 11 — and RF06 — build unit 6 of 11)*
502:- **RNF06 (architecture):** Zero Clean Architecture layer violations — the domain layer imports neither `package:flutter` nor anything from a `data/` layer, in any of the 11 feature modules.
538:*Addendum: `addendum.md` in this folder holds implementation-level decisions (routing, HTTP client, local cache, DI, package choices and rejected alternatives), competitive-landscape and market-sizing detail, regulatory citations, and corrections-carried-forward from prior planning sessions — none of it duplicated here.*

entries.name: WebFetch
entries.description:
IMPORTANT: WebFetch WILL FAIL for authenticated or private URLs. Before using this tool, check if the URL points to an authenticated service (e.g. Google Docs, Confluence, Jira, GitHub). If so, look for a specialized MCP tool that provides authenticated access.
- claude.ai artifact links (claude.ai/artifact/{id} or claude.ai/code/artifact/{uuid}, including preview.claude.ai) are published artifacts: read them with the Artifact tool (action "read"), not WebFetch, curl or a headless browser.

- Fetches content from a specified URL and processes it using an AI model
- Takes a URL and a prompt as input
- Fetches the URL content, converts HTML to markdown
- Processes the content with the prompt using a small, fast model
- Returns the model's response about the content
- Use this tool when you need to retrieve and analyze web content

Usage notes:
  - IMPORTANT: If an MCP-provided web fetch tool is available, prefer using that tool instead of this one, as it may have fewer restrictions.
  - The URL must be a fully-formed valid URL
  - HTTP URLs will be automatically upgraded to HTTPS
  - localhost and other hostnames without a dot are not supported; for a local server, use curl via Bash
  - The prompt should describe what information you want to extract from the page
  - This tool is read-only and does not modify any files
  - Results may be summarized if the content is very large
  - Includes a self-cleaning cache (entries expire after 15 minutes) for faster responses when repeatedly accessing the same URL
  - When a URL redirects to a different host, the tool will inform you and provide the redirect URL in a special format. You should then make a new WebFetch request with the redirect URL to fetch the content.
  - For GitHub URLs, prefer using the gh CLI via Bash instead (e.g., gh pr view, gh issue view, gh api).

url.description: The URL to fetch content from

prompt.description: The prompt to run on the fetched content

entries.name: WebSearch
entries.description:
- Allows Claude to search the web and use the results to inform responses
- Provides up-to-date information for current events and recent data
- Returns search result information formatted as search result blocks, including links as markdown hyperlinks
- Use this tool for accessing information beyond Claude's knowledge cutoff
- Searches are performed automatically within a single API call

CRITICAL REQUIREMENT - You MUST follow this:
  - After answering the user's question, you MUST include a "Sources:" section at the end of your response
  - In the Sources section, list all relevant URLs from the search results as markdown hyperlinks: [Title](URL)
  - This is MANDATORY - never skip including sources in your response
  - Example format:

    [Your answer here]

    Sources:
    - [Source Title 1](https://example.com/1)
    - [Source Title 2](https://example.com/2)

Usage notes:
  - Domain filtering is supported to include or block specific websites
  - Web search is only available in the US

IMPORTANT - Use the correct year in search queries:
  - The current month is October 2026. You MUST use this year when searching for recent information, documentation, or current events.
  - Example: If the user asks for "latest React docs", search for "React documentation" with the current year, NOT last year

allowed_domains.description: Only include search results from these domains

blocked_domains.description: Never include search results from these domains

mode.description: "standard": the normal web search: quick and cheap; right for straightforward lookups (reference facts, official pages, documentation, well-known people, places and topics) and simple follow-up lookups. "extended": a thorough, fresh search at several times the cost and latency.

constraint	Platform: iOS only, portrait orientation only (requirements.md sec.13). No Android target, no landscape layout work.
constraint	Clean Architecture, 3 layers per feature (data/domain/presentation) under lib/features/<feature>/; domain imports neither package:flutter nor anything from data/ (RNF06, AGENTS.md).
constraint	State management fixed: flutter_bloc. Error handling fixed: fpdart Either<Failure,T> on every repository signature, no exceptions. Test doubles fixed: mocktail. On-device STT fixed: whisper_ggml (audio never reaches backend).
constraint	Backend is frozen and out of scope: every call goes to {FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL}/<x-cerne-function>, never the literal openapi.yaml REST path. apikey header on every call; Authorization: Bearer <anon key> only on signup/login/refresh (security: [] ops); Authorization: Bearer <user token> on every bearerAuth op.
constraint	Visual tokens: lib/core/design_tokens.dart is the single source for every color/font/spacing/radius (RNF08); never write a visual value elsewhere.
constraint	RF10: chat feature must create entries through a shared interface/use case, never by importing the entries repository or data source directly (violating this also breaks RNF06).
constraint	RF07: no BLoC imports another BLoC directly; the auth/sync/data streams it composes combine only through the domain layer.
constraint	Entries are immutable once created: no PATCH/DELETE /entries/:id in the backend contract; no screen offers edit or delete of an entry.
constraint	Architecture is cloud-only: offline permits viewing already-cached data only, never writing (RF06 AC, generalized across all write endpoints per requirements.md sec.6 note on POST /chat/sessions and /chat/.../messages being "blocked offline").
constraint	Sync badge has no server column: computed entirely client-side from Entry.serverRevision + Entry.updatedAt + transient pending-local-write state (sync-badge.md). Server never supplies a sync_status field.
constraint	Minimum domain-layer test coverage >=80% (RNF07); 5 write endpoints x 3 failure types (timeout, malformed response, no connection) = 15 scenarios covered by mocktail tests (RNF09).
decision	[ADOPTED] Local cache: Hive family, 3 Hive boxes (entries by id, chat_messages by session id, chat_sessions by id) + one pagination cursor string. No relational engine: every query dimension (source/dateFrom/dateTo, semantic search) is a server-side query param per openapi.yaml; the client never filters/joins/sorts cached data itself. Source: F000 forge session 2026-10-25.
event	CORRECTION to F000 forge session: the forge locked package "Hive" (hive + hive_flutter, last published 2022, four years stale as of this run). Web-verified 2026-10-26: upstream Hive is unmaintained; hive_ce (https://pub.dev/packages/hive_ce) is the actively maintained continuation, API-compatible box/adapter model, latest 2.22.0 published 12 days ago, requires Dart 3. Spine adopts hive_ce in place of hive/hive_flutter; the 3-box cache shape and "no client-side filter/join/sort" rule from the forge session are unchanged and carry over as-is.
decision	[ADOPTED] Vault: flutter_secure_storage (plain, non-biometric-gated PIN-hash item) + local_auth (Face ID/Touch ID), both owned by one vault state machine. Rejected biometric_storage: gating storage behind biometric success cannot satisfy RF03's "biometric failure falls back to PIN without lockout" (checking the PIN would need the hash, which would need biometric success -- circular). Zero Either/Failure plumbing: 100% local, no backend call (backend README confirms no biometric-unlock endpoint). Source: F000 forge session 2026-10-25.
decision	[ADOPTED] DI: plain get_it, no injectable/codegen. Each feature exposes one registerXFeature(GetIt it) function called from main.dart. A feature registers its own BLoCs/use cases/repositories/data sources, plus the domain-layer interfaces (ports) it exposes for other features to consume. Source: F000 forge session 2026-10-25, generalized here for cross-feature registration order.
decision	[ADOPTED] DTOs/domain entities: freezed + json_serializable, justified by field count (Entry has 11 required fields per openapi.yaml) and sealed unions (Failure, Resource) -- not blanket codegen on every class. Source: F000 forge session 2026-10-25.
decision	[ADOPTED] Routing: go_router, single redirect callback keyed off one SessionStatus stream; no screen independently checks auth state or opts out of the gate. Source: F000 forge session 2026-10-25.

# Architecture Spine — Cerne

## Design Paradigm

**Clean Architecture, 3 layers per feature, BLoC on top, errors carried as values.**

- `presentation/` (BLoC/Cubit + widgets) → depends on → `domain/` (entities, use cases, repository/port interfaces) ← implemented by ← `data/` (DTOs, data sources, repository implementations).
- `domain/` is the only layer every other layer may depend on; it depends on nothing feature-specific and never on `package:flutter` (RNF06).
- Every operation that can fail (network, parse, local I/O) returns `Either<Failure, T>` (`fpdart`) at the repository boundary — no repository throws past itself (RNF09).
- `core/` sits beneath every feature and holds the only cross-feature-shared code: the `Failure` hierarchy, the API client/URL builder, the DI bootstrap, the local-cache boxes, `Resource<T>`, `isolatedSideEffect`, design tokens, and the `SessionStatus` contract.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph Feature["any lib/features/<name>/"]
        P["presentation (BLoC/Cubit, widgets)"]
        D["domain (entities, use cases, port interfaces)"]
        DA["data (DTOs, data sources, repository impl)"]
        P --> D
        DA --> D
    end
    Core["core/ (Failure, ApiClient, DI, cache, Resource<T>, SessionStatus, design_tokens)"]
    Feature --> Core
    OtherDomain["another feature's domain/ (port interfaces only)"]
    P -.->|"AD-6: cross-feature calls only through the owning feature's domain port"| OtherDomain
```

## Invariants & Rules

### AD-1 — Layer dependency direction (RNF06)

- **Binds:** all features
- **Prevents:** `domain/` depending on Flutter, on any `data/` (own or another feature's), or on another feature's `presentation/`.
- **Rule:** dependency direction is strictly `presentation → domain ← data`. `domain/` imports neither `package:flutter` nor anything under any `data/`. Only `data/` imports `dio`/`hive_ce`/platform plugins. `presentation/` never imports a feature's own or another feature's `data/` directly.

### AD-2 — Either-everywhere error channel (RNF09)

- **Binds:** all repositories (read and write)
- **Prevents:** a feature inventing its own error signaling (exceptions crossing the repository boundary, nullable returns, ad hoc string errors) that other code can't pattern-match generically.
- **Rule:** every repository method returns `Future<Either<Failure, T>>` (or `Stream<Either<Failure, T>>` for the chat SSE stream). `Failure` is the closed hierarchy in AD-3. No repository implementation lets a native/dio exception escape unmapped.

### AD-3 — Closed `Failure` hierarchy `[ADOPTED]`

- **Binds:** all
- **Prevents:** two features inventing different shapes for "network timeout," or silently dropping one of the server's 13 codes.
- **Rule:** one sealed `Failure` class in `core/`, exactly 14 subtypes — the 13 from `error-taxonomy.md` (`AuthExpired`, `AuthInvalid`, `NetworkTimeout`, `NetworkOffline`, `Validation`, `PiiCheckFailed`, `EmbeddingFailed`, `AiGenerationTimeout`, `NotFound`, `RateLimited`, `ExportEmptyPeriod`, `PayloadTooLarge`, `OcrNoText`) plus the local-only `MalformedResponse` (`retryable` hardcoded `false`, for the client's own parse-failure detection). Never redefined or subset per feature.

### AD-4 — Retry policy lives in exactly one place `[ADOPTED]`

- **Binds:** the API client
- **Prevents:** a feature writing its own retry loop that double-retries, or retries a `retryable:false` code.
- **Rule:** retry logic is implemented once (the `dio` interceptor / `ApiClient` wrapper), fires only for the 6 server `retryable:true` codes (`NETWORK_TIMEOUT`, `NETWORK_OFFLINE`, `PII_CHECK_FAILED`, `EMBEDDING_FAILED`, `AI_GENERATION_TIMEOUT`, `RATE_LIMITED`). Every other code surfaces once, unretried.

### AD-5 — Function-name URL construction and header policy

- **Binds:** every network call
- **Prevents:** a feature string-concatenating the literal `openapi.yaml` REST path (which is not a real URL) or re-deciding which `Authorization` value to send.
- **Rule:** one URL builder in `core/` maps each operation to `{FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL}/<x-cerne-function>/<path-params>`. One `dio` interceptor owns headers: `apikey` on every call; `Authorization: Bearer <anon key>` only on the three `security: []` operations (signup, login, refresh); `Authorization: Bearer <user token>` on every other (`bearerAuth`) operation.

### AD-6 — Cross-feature access only through a domain-layer port

- **Binds:** RF10 (chat → entries), and any future cross-feature dependency
- **Prevents:** a feature reaching into another feature's `data/`, repository, data source, or BLoC — the exact violation RF10's acceptance criteria calls out, which would also break RNF06.
- **Rule:** the *owning* feature defines an abstract use case/port in its own `domain/` (e.g. `entries/domain` exposes `SaveEntryUseCase`) and registers the concrete implementation in its own DI registration function. A *consuming* feature (e.g. `chat`) only ever imports and injects that abstract type from the owning feature's `domain/` — never anything from its `data/` or `presentation/`.

### AD-7 — No BLoC-to-BLoC references

- **Binds:** all (generalizes RF07's explicit AC to every feature)
- **Prevents:** hidden coupling and circular-rebuild chains between presentation units built independently.
- **Rule:** a BLoC/Cubit constructor never takes another BLoC/Cubit as a dependency, same-feature or cross-feature. Composition of multiple independent state sources happens by injecting the underlying `domain/` streams/use-cases into each BLoC independently, or via `BlocListener`/`MultiBlocListener` in the widget tree — never a direct BLoC → BLoC reference.

### AD-8 — Single `SessionStatus` source of truth

- **Binds:** F000 (go_router redirect), RF07 (composite auth × sync × data state), any feature that needs session validity
- **Prevents:** two independently-built screens disagreeing on what "session expired" means or when to prompt re-login.
- **Rule:** exactly one `SessionStatus` stream, exposed from the auth feature's `domain/`, registered once in DI as a singleton. Every consumer injects/listens to that stream; none re-derives session state from a raw 401, from its own `GET /auth/session` poll, or from a second stream.

### AD-9 — Cloud-only: no offline write queue

- **Binds:** all repositories (generalizes RF06's "cloud-only" note and RF04's "blocked offline" writes)
- **Prevents:** a feature building a local write-queue/outbox that silently diverges from "offline permits viewing cached data only."
- **Rule:** a write attempted with no connectivity resolves immediately to `Either.left(Failure.networkOffline)` — it is never queued for later. Read operations transparently fall back to the local `hive_ce` cache. The only client-side "pending write" state is transient, in-memory, scoped to one in-flight request (it feeds AD-10's `Synchronizing` badge state) — it is never persisted as a queue.

### AD-10 — Sync badge is a pure client-side derivation (locks `sync-badge.md`)

- **Binds:** every screen that renders the per-entry sync badge (chat save confirmation, My Records list, any future one)
- **Prevents:** two screens computing `Synchronizing`/`Error`/`Synchronized` differently.
- **Rule:** one derivation function lives in `entries/domain`, computed from `Entry.serverRevision` + `Entry.updatedAt` + the transient pending-write flag (AD-9). Every screen consumes that function's output; none recomputes the badge inline. The server never supplies a `sync_status` field — `requirements.md` §8 is wrong on this point (`sync-badge.md` and the `Entry` schema win).

### AD-11 — Entry immutability

- **Binds:** the entries feature
- **Prevents:** a unit speculatively adding an update/delete path the backend doesn't support.
- **Rule:** `EntriesRepository` exposes create and read operations only. No update or delete method is ever added, matching the backend's lack of `PATCH`/`DELETE /entries/:id`.

### AD-12 — Shared view-state scoped to single-source-of-truth fetches `[ADOPTED]`

- **Binds:** RF06 (search results), RF09 (dashboard aggregate/narrative) — explicitly *not* RF02 or RF07
- **Prevents:** forcing a composite or multi-stage state machine into a generic fetch enum, and the reverse: ad hoc one-off state shapes where a shared one would do.
- **Rule:** generic `Resource<T>` (`idle`/`loading`/`data`/`error`) lives in `core/`, used only by screens with one data source and one fetch lifecycle. RF02's capture pipeline (`recording`/`processing`/`transcribed`/`error`) and RF07's composite auth × sync × data state each define their own sealed state class — never forced into `Resource<T>`.

### AD-13 — `isolatedSideEffect` contract fixed now, implementation deferred `[ADOPTED]`

- **Binds:** RF08, RF10 (both state the identical failure-isolation requirement)
- **Rule:** `core/` holds a never-throws helper with signature `Future<Either<Failure, T>> Function(Future<T> Function())`-shaped (never throws past itself); it ships with RF10, delivery order's first consumer (RF04 → RF10 → RF08), not built speculatively in F000. RF08 reuses it from `core/` without a cross-feature import.

## Consistency Conventions

| Concern | Convention |
| --- | --- |
| Feature naming | `lib/features/<feature>/` one of: `auth`, `vault`, `capture`, `entries`, `chat`, `export`, `dashboard`, `account` — see Capability → Architecture Map |
| Errors | `Failure` sealed hierarchy (AD-3) everywhere; UI maps a `Failure` to copy using its `retryable` flag, never a hardcoded per-screen message list |
| IDs & dates | server-assigned string IDs and ISO-8601 timestamps passed through verbatim from DTOs (`freezed`+`json_serializable`); the client never generates or reformats an entity ID |
| Visual values | `lib/core/design_tokens.dart` only (RNF08) — no color/font/spacing/radius literal anywhere else |
| Network envelope | one `ApiClient`/URL-builder + one header interceptor (AD-5); no feature constructs a request URL or header set itself |
| State composition | `Resource<T>` for single-source fetches (AD-12); no BLoC-to-BLoC references (AD-7) |
| Testing | `mocktail` stubs one `ApiClient` interface per repository test, not a fake transport layer; one shared table-driven helper drives the 5-write-endpoints × 3-failure-types = 15-scenario matrix (RNF09); ≥80% line coverage gate on every `domain/` (RNF07) |
| Config/secrets | `.env` (`FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL`, `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`) loaded via `flutter_dotenv`; never committed, never hardcoded |
| AI provider access | the app never calls Claude or Voyage AI directly — every AI-backed feature goes through the backend's documented endpoints (project policy, binding on all features) |

## Stack

| freezed + freezed_annotation | ^4.0.3 |

| whisper_ggml | ^2.8.1 |

## Structural Seed

```text
lib/
  core/
    design_tokens.dart        # RNF08 — the only source of color/font/spacing/radius
    network/                  # ApiClient, URL builder, header + retry interceptor (AD-4, AD-5)
```

23	
24	# Architecture Spine — Cerne
25	
26	## Design Paradigm
27	
28	**Clean Architecture, 3 layers per feature, BLoC on top, errors carried as values.**
29	
30	- `presentation/` (BLoC/Cubit + widgets) → depends on → `domain/` (entities, use cases, repository/port interfaces) ← implemented by ← `data/` (DTOs, data sources, repository implementations).
31	- `domain/` is the only layer every other layer may depend on; it depends on nothing feature-specific and never on `package:flutter` (RNF06).
32	- Every operation that can fail (network, parse, local I/O) returns `Either<Failure, T>` (`fpdart`) at the repository boundary — no repository throws past itself (RNF09).
33	- `core/` sits beneath every feature and holds the only cross-feature-shared code: the `Failure` hierarchy, the API client/URL builder, the DI bootstrap, the local-cache boxes, `Resource<T>`, `isolatedSideEffect`, design tokens, and the `SessionStatus` contract.
34	
35	```mermaid
36	flowchart TD
37	    subgraph Feature["any lib/features/<name>/"]
38	        P["presentation (BLoC/Cubit, widgets)"]
39	        D["domain (entities, use cases, port interfaces)"]
40	        DA["data (DTOs, data sources, repository impl)"]
41	        P --> D
42	        DA --> D
43	    end
44	    Core["core/ (Failure, ApiClient, DI, cache, Resource<T>, SessionStatus, design_tokens)"]
45	    Feature --> Core
46	    OtherDomain["another feature's domain/ (port interfaces only)"]
47	    P -.->|"AD-6: cross-feature calls only through the owning feature's domain port"| OtherDomain
48	```
49	
50	## Invariants & Rules
51	
52	### AD-1 — Layer dependency direction (RNF06)
53	
54	- **Binds:** all features
55	- **Prevents:** `domain/` depending on Flutter, on any `data/` (own or another feature's), or on another feature's `presentation/`.
56	- **Rule:** dependency direction is strictly `presentation → domain ← data`. `domain/` imports neither `package:flutter` nor anything under any `data/`. Only `data/` imports `dio`/`hive_ce`/platform plugins. `presentation/` never imports a feature's own or another feature's `data/` directly.
57	
58	### AD-2 — Either-everywhere error channel (RNF09)
59	
60	- **Binds:** all repositories (read and write)
61	- **Prevents:** a feature inventing its own error signaling (exceptions crossing the repository boundary, nullable returns, ad hoc string errors) that other code can't pattern-match generically.
62	- **Rule:** every repository method returns `Future<Either<Failure, T>>` (or `Stream<Either<Failure, T>>` for the chat SSE stream). `Failure` is the closed hierarchy in AD-3. No repository implementation lets a native/dio exception escape unmapped.
63	
64	### AD-3 — Closed `Failure` hierarchy `[ADOPTED]`
65	
66	- **Binds:** all
67	- **Prevents:** two features inventing different shapes for "network timeout," or silently dropping one of the server's 13 codes.
68	- **Rule:** one sealed `Failure` class in `core/`, exactly 14 subtypes — the 13 from `error-taxonomy.md` (`AuthExpired`, `AuthInvalid`, `NetworkTimeout`, `NetworkOffline`, `Validation`, `PiiCheckFailed`, `EmbeddingFailed`, `AiGenerationTimeout`, `NotFound`, `RateLimited`, `ExportEmptyPeriod`, `PayloadTooLarge`, `OcrNoText`) plus the local-only `MalformedResponse` (`retryable` hardcoded `false`, for the client's own parse-failure detection). Never redefined or subset per feature.
69	
70	### AD-4 — Retry policy lives in exactly one place `[ADOPTED]`
71	
72	- **Binds:** the API client
73	- **Prevents:** a feature writing its own retry loop that double-retries, or retries a `retryable:false` code.
74	- **Rule:** retry logic is implemented once (the `dio` interceptor / `ApiClient` wrapper), fires only for the 6 server `retryable:true` codes (`NETWORK_TIMEOUT`, `NETWORK_OFFLINE`, `PII_CHECK_FAILED`, `EMBEDDING_FAILED`, `AI_GENERATION_TIMEOUT`, `RATE_LIMITED`). Every other code surfaces once, unretried.
75	
76	### AD-5 — Function-name URL construction and header policy
77	
78	- **Binds:** every network call
79	- **Prevents:** a feature string-concatenating the literal `openapi.yaml` REST path (which is not a real URL) or re-deciding which `Authorization` value to send.
80	- **Rule:** one URL builder in `core/` maps each operation to `{FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL}/<x-cerne-function>/<path-params>`. One `dio` interceptor owns headers: `apikey` on every call; `Authorization: Bearer <anon key>` only on the three `security: []` operations (signup, login, refresh); `Authorization: Bearer <user token>` on every other (`bearerAuth`) operation.
81	
82	### AD-6 — Cross-feature access only through a domain-layer port
83	
84	- **Binds:** RF10 (chat → entries), and any future cross-feature dependency
85	- **Prevents:** a feature reaching into another feature's `data/`, repository, data source, or BLoC — the exact violation RF10's acceptance criteria calls out, which would also break RNF06.
86	- **Rule:** the *owning* feature defines an abstract use case/port in its own `domain/` (e.g. `entries/domain` exposes `SaveEntryUseCase`) and registers the concrete implementation in its own DI registration function. A *consuming* feature (e.g. `chat`) only ever imports and injects that abstract type from the owning feature's `domain/` — never anything from its `data/` or `presentation/`.
87	
88	### AD-7 — No BLoC-to-BLoC references
89	
90	- **Binds:** all (generalizes RF07's explicit AC to every feature)
91	- **Prevents:** hidden coupling and circular-rebuild chains between presentation units built independently.
92	- **Rule:** a BLoC/Cubit constructor never takes another BLoC/Cubit as a dependency, same-feature or cross-feature. Composition of multiple independent state sources happens by injecting the underlying `domain/` streams/use-cases into each BLoC independently, or via `BlocListener`/`MultiBlocListener` in the widget tree — never a direct BLoC → BLoC reference.
93	
94	### AD-8 — Single `SessionStatus` source of truth
95	
96	- **Binds:** F000 (go_router redirect), RF07 (composite auth × sync × data state), any feature that needs session validity
97	- **Prevents:** two independently-built screens disagreeing on what "session expired" means or when to prompt re-login.
98	- **Rule:** exactly one `SessionStatus` stream, exposed from the auth feature's `domain/`, registered once in DI as a singleton. Every consumer injects/listens to that stream; none re-derives session state from a raw 401, from its own `GET /auth/session` poll, or from a second stream.
99	
100	### AD-9 — Cloud-only: no offline write queue
101	
102	- **Binds:** all repositories (generalizes RF06's "cloud-only" note and RF04's "blocked offline" writes)
103	- **Prevents:** a feature building a local write-queue/outbox that silently diverges from "offline permits viewing cached data only."
104	- **Rule:** a write attempted with no connectivity resolves immediately to `Either.left(Failure.networkOffline)` — it is never queued for later. Read operations transparently fall back to the local `hive_ce` cache. The only client-side "pending write" state is transient, in-memory, scoped to one in-flight request (it feeds AD-10's `Synchronizing` badge state) — it is never persisted as a queue.
105	
106	### AD-10 — Sync badge is a pure client-side derivation (locks `sync-badge.md`)
107	
108	- **Binds:** every screen that renders the per-entry sync badge (chat save confirmation, My Records list, any future one)
109	- **Prevents:** two screens computing `Synchronizing`/`Error`/`Synchronized` differently.
110	- **Rule:** one derivation function lives in `entries/domain`, computed from `Entry.serverRevision` + `Entry.updatedAt` + the transient pending-write flag (AD-9). Every screen consumes that function's output; none recomputes the badge inline. The server never supplies a `sync_status` field — `requirements.md` §8 is wrong on this point (`sync-badge.md` and the `Entry` schema win).
111	
112	### AD-11 — Entry immutability
113	
114	- **Binds:** the entries feature
115	- **Prevents:** a unit speculatively adding an update/delete path the backend doesn't support.
116	- **Rule:** `EntriesRepository` exposes create and read operations only. No update or delete method is ever added, matching the backend's lack of `PATCH`/`DELETE /entries/:id`.
117	
118	### AD-12 — Shared view-state scoped to single-source-of-truth fetches `[ADOPTED]`
119	
120	- **Binds:** RF06 (search results), RF09 (dashboard aggregate/narrative) — explicitly *not* RF02 or RF07
121	- **Prevents:** forcing a composite or multi-stage state machine into a generic fetch enum, and the reverse: ad hoc one-off state shapes where a shared one would do.
122	- **Rule:** generic `Resource<T>` (`idle`/`loading`/`data`/`error`) lives in `core/`, used only by screens with one data source and one fetch lifecycle. RF02's capture pipeline (`recording`/`processing`/`transcribed`/`error`) and RF07's composite auth × sync × data state each define their own sealed state class — never forced into `Resource<T>`.
123	
124	### AD-13 — `isolatedSideEffect` contract fixed now, implementation deferred `[ADOPTED]`
125	
126	- **Binds:** RF08, RF10 (both state the identical failure-isolation requirement)
127	- **Prevents:** RF08 reinventing its own failure-isolation wrapper (or importing RF10's feature-local one), producing two incompatible "never block the caller on failure" implementations.
128	- **Rule:** `core/` holds a never-throws helper with signature `Future<Either<Failure, T>> Function(Future<T> Function())`-shaped (never throws past itself); it ships with RF10, delivery order's first consumer (RF04 → RF10 → RF08), not built speculatively in F000. RF08 reuses it from `core/` without a cross-feature import.
129	
130	## Consistency Conventions
131	
132	| Concern | Convention |
133	| --- | --- |
134	| Feature naming | `lib/features/<feature>/` one of: `auth`, `vault`, `capture`, `entries`, `chat`, `export`, `dashboard`, `account` — see Capability → Architecture Map |
135	| Errors | `Failure` sealed hierarchy (AD-3) everywhere; UI maps a `Failure` to copy using its `retryable` flag, never a hardcoded per-screen message list |
136	| IDs & dates | server-assigned string IDs and ISO-8601 timestamps passed through verbatim from DTOs (`freezed`+`json_serializable`); the client never generates or reformats an entity ID |
137	| Visual values | `lib/core/design_tokens.dart` only (RNF08) — no color/font/spacing/radius literal anywhere else |

139	| State composition | `Resource<T>` for single-source fetches (AD-12); no BLoC-to-BLoC references (AD-7) |
